quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Class 5B went to the science museum on Tuesday. They watched a short film about space, touched a real meteorite and built small rockets from paper. The children talked about the trip all the way back to school.
options: A class had an exciting day at the science museum.
The children built small rockets out of paper during the visit.
A real meteorite was taken to the school for the children.
The children talked about space on the long bus ride home.
quests.correctAnswer: A class had an exciting day at the science museum.
quests.hint: A trip has many moments. Which option describes the trip itself rather than one moment in it?
quests.explanation: The film, the meteorite and the rockets are all parts of one museum visit, and the children's talk afterwards shows they enjoyed it. Choosing a single activity would leave out most of the day.
keyPoints: Class 5B spent Tuesday at a science museum.
They watched a film, touched a meteorite and built paper rockets.
The children kept talking about the trip on the way home.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Wei took his grandmother to the hospital for her check-up. The waiting room was crowded, so they sat for almost an hour. The doctor was kind, and the news was good.
options: Wei's grandmother is ill and must stay in hospital for a week.
Wei's grandmother had a long wait but a good check-up.
Wei works at the hospital where his grandmother is a patient.
The hospital waiting room was crowded for almost an hour.
quests.correctAnswer: Wei's grandmother had a long wait but a good check-up.
quests.hint: Check whether your choice covers how the visit began and how it ended.
quests.explanation: The paragraph moves from a slow wait to a positive result. A summary about only the crowded room would miss the good news that closes the story.
keyPoints: Wei brought his grandmother to the hospital for a check-up.
They had to wait nearly an hour in a crowded room.
The doctor was kind and gave them good news.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Camila's friends planned a surprise party for her sixteenth birthday. They hid the cake at a neighbour's house and told her they were going to the cinema. When she walked into the room, everyone shouted her name.
options: Camila organised a party for her friends' birthdays.
A neighbour kept a cake at her house for a week.
Camila and her friends went to the cinema together.
Camila's friends surprised her with a birthday party.
quests.correctAnswer: Camila's friends surprised her with a birthday party.
quests.hint: Think about who planned what, and who was surprised. Watch for options that swap the roles.
quests.explanation: Her friends planned the event and Camila was the surprised guest of honour. The cinema story was only a cover, and the cake was one of the preparations.
keyPoints: Camila's friends planned a surprise for her sixteenth birthday.
They hid the cake and pretended they were going to the cinema.
Camila was surprised when everyone shouted her name.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Lakeview Café sits on a quiet corner near the station. It serves hot soup and fresh bread at lunchtime, and there are plants on every table. Many office workers come in for a peaceful break.
options: A busy café near the station is always full at breakfast.
A café near the station sells only soup and fresh bread.
A calm café near the station gives office workers a pleasant lunch break.
Office workers grow the plants that decorate a station café.
quests.correctAnswer: A calm café near the station gives office workers a pleasant lunch break.
quests.hint: For a description of a place, ask what the place is like and who uses it.
quests.explanation: The corner, the food and the plants all create a peaceful place, and the office workers show who enjoys it. The menu is one detail among several.
keyPoints: Lakeview Café is on a quiet corner near the station.
It offers soup, bread and plants that create a calm feeling.
Office workers come there for a peaceful break.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The old fort on the hill has thick stone walls and a wide view of the sea. Visitors can climb its towers on sunny days. A small museum inside tells the story of the town.
options: A small museum inside the fort is closed on sunny days.
The old fort has thick stone walls that face the sea.
The town began when people built a fort on the hill.
The old fort is worth visiting for its views and its history.
quests.correctAnswer: The old fort is worth visiting for its views and its history.
quests.hint: Look for the idea that links the walls, the towers and the museum.
quests.explanation: Views from the towers and history in the museum are two reasons a visitor would go. The stone walls are only one physical feature.
keyPoints: The fort stands on a hill above the sea.
Visitors can climb the towers for wide views.
A small museum inside explains the town's history.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Green Street Park has a playground, a pond and a running track. Families go there at weekends, and joggers arrive early each morning. Volunteers keep the flowerbeds neat.
options: Volunteers spend every weekend planting flowers in the park.
Families and joggers both enjoy what a local park offers.
Joggers at Green Street Park arrive early to use the playground.
The pond is the most popular place for families to meet.
quests.correctAnswer: Families and joggers both enjoy what a local park offers.
quests.hint: Cross out options that give one person or one place more importance than the paragraph does.
quests.explanation: The park suits different visitors: families use it at weekends and joggers use it in the morning. The volunteers and flowerbeds are supporting information.
keyPoints: Green Street Park has a playground, pond and running track.
Families visit at weekends and joggers come in the mornings.
Volunteers keep the flowerbeds neat.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Tariq lost his wallet on the bus. He called the bus company, and a driver had found it under a seat. Tariq collected it the next morning, and nothing was missing.
options: A bus driver gave Tariq money for a new wallet.
Tariq lost his wallet on a crowded bus.
Tariq got his lost wallet back from the bus company.
Tariq's wallet was found empty under a bus seat.
quests.correctAnswer: Tariq got his lost wallet back from the bus company.
quests.hint: A problem paragraph is not complete until you know how it ended.
quests.explanation: The paragraph starts with a problem, the lost wallet, and ends with a happy solution. An answer that mentions only the loss leaves out the resolution.
keyPoints: Tariq lost his wallet on the bus.
He called the bus company, and a driver had found it.
He collected it the next morning with nothing missing.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The kitchen tap at Rosa's flat kept dripping all night. She watched a short video, bought a small rubber ring at the hardware store and fitted it herself. The dripping stopped, and the tap works well now.
options: Rosa fixed a dripping tap herself with a small part.
Rosa called a plumber to repair the dripping tap.
Rosa bought a whole new tap at the hardware store.
Rosa learned how to make videos about kitchen taps.
quests.correctAnswer: Rosa fixed a dripping tap herself with a small part.
quests.hint: Match the problem to the solution. Which option keeps them connected?
quests.explanation: The tap was dripping, and Rosa solved it herself by learning and fitting a small part. Options that change who did the repair or what she bought go against the passage.
keyPoints: Rosa's kitchen tap dripped all night.
She learned what to do from a video and bought a rubber ring.
She fitted it herself and stopped the dripping.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The school bus was late three times last week, so students missed their first lessons. Parents wrote to the bus company, and the company added a second bus on the same route. Now students arrive on time.
options: The bus company replaced its old bus with a bigger one.
Parents wrote to the school and asked for later lessons.
A school bus was late three times last week.
Parents' complaints led to an extra bus that ended the lateness.
quests.correctAnswer: Parents' complaints led to an extra bus that ended the lateness.
quests.hint: Trace the chain from the problem to the action to the result.
quests.explanation: The lateness caused the complaint, the complaint caused the change, and the change fixed the problem. An answer that stops at the late bus is only the beginning of the story.
keyPoints: The school bus was often late, and students missed lessons.
Parents wrote to the bus company about it.
The company added a second bus, so students now arrive on time.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Mrs. Aziz keeps her spare key with a neighbour. Last winter she locked herself out on a freezing evening, and it took two hours to find a locksmith. She does not want that to happen again.
options: Mrs. Aziz now leaves a spare key with a neighbour because she was locked out once.
Mrs. Aziz's neighbour often locks himself out of his flat.
Mrs. Aziz plans to change all the locks on her door.
Mrs. Aziz waited two hours for a locksmith last winter.
quests.correctAnswer: Mrs. Aziz now leaves a spare key with a neighbour because she was locked out once.
quests.hint: Ask why the person acts this way. The paragraph gives the answer in the middle.
quests.explanation: The habit of leaving a key with a neighbour makes sense because of the lockout last winter. A summary of only the lockout would leave out what she now does about it.
keyPoints: Mrs. Aziz leaves her spare key with a neighbour.
Last winter she was locked out and waited two hours for help.
She wants to avoid the same trouble in the future.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Jin wears a bright badge on his backpack because he is a student guide at the university. New students often feel lost in their first week. The badge helps them see who is happy to answer questions.
options: Jin's backpack is very bright, so new students notice him.
Jin is a new student who feels lost during his first week.
A student guide wears a badge so new students can find help.
Jin gives badges to every new student at the university.
quests.correctAnswer: A student guide wears a badge so new students can find help.
quests.hint: Which option explains the reason for the badge, not just the badge itself?
quests.explanation: The badge has a purpose: it lets nervous new students spot a friendly guide. Options that change Jin's role or the badge's job misread the paragraph.
keyPoints: Jin is a student guide at the university.
New students often feel lost in their first week.
His badge shows them who is willing to help.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whenever it is sunny, Pilar hangs her washing outside instead of using the dryer. It saves electricity, and she likes the fresh smell of the clothes. Her monthly bill has become smaller.
options: Pilar's dryer is broken, so she washes everything by hand.
Pilar's electricity bill is too high for her to pay.
Pilar likes the fresh smell of her clothes.
Pilar dries clothes outside on sunny days to save electricity.
quests.correctAnswer: Pilar dries clothes outside on sunny days to save electricity.
quests.hint: When several reasons are given, find the one that connects to the result.
quests.explanation: Her habit of drying outdoors reduces her electricity use, which explains the smaller bill. The pleasant smell is a bonus, not the main reason.
keyPoints: Pilar dries her washing outside when the weather is sunny.
This saves electricity compared with using a dryer.
As a result, her monthly bill is smaller.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Two years ago, the old cinema on Bridge Road was empty and dark. A local family bought it, painted the walls and added comfortable seats. Now it shows films every evening and is often full.
options: A local family sold their cinema on Bridge Road.
The cinema on Bridge Road shows films only at weekends.
A family's repairs turned an empty cinema into a busy one.
Comfortable seats were the reason the cinema closed.
quests.correctAnswer: A family's repairs turned an empty cinema into a busy one.
quests.hint: For a paragraph about change, compare the beginning with the end.
quests.explanation: The contrast between an empty, dark cinema and a full, active one is the point. The new seats are just one of the changes that helped.
keyPoints: The cinema on Bridge Road used to be empty.
A local family bought it, painted it and added seats.
It now shows films every evening and is often full.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Petra used to walk to work, but the trip took forty minutes. Last month she bought a folding scooter, and now she gets there in fifteen. She says her mornings feel much less rushed.
options: A scooter shortened Petra's journey and made her mornings easier.
Petra folds her scooter and takes it on the train.
Petra rides a scooter because her car has broken down.
Petra walks to work for forty minutes every day.
quests.correctAnswer: A scooter shortened Petra's journey and made her mornings easier.
quests.hint: Notice what changed and what improved. A good summary covers both.
quests.explanation: Petra changed how she travels, and the result was a faster trip and calmer mornings. Talking only about the old walk reverses the passage's direction.
keyPoints: Petra once walked forty minutes to work.
She now uses a folding scooter and arrives in fifteen.
Her mornings feel much less rushed.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The village well used to be the only place to get water, and children spent hours carrying buckets. Since new pipes arrived, every house has a tap. The children now have more time to study and play.
options: The village well is still the main source of water.
New pipes freed village children from hours of carrying water.
The children now spend hours studying every day.
Every house in the village dug its own well.
quests.correctAnswer: New pipes freed village children from hours of carrying water.
quests.hint: Look at what life was like before and after. What caused the difference?
quests.explanation: Water pipes replaced the well, and that gave children time back. Answers about the well alone miss the change and its effect on the children.
keyPoints: The village once depended on one well for water.
New pipes brought a tap to every house.
Children no longer spend hours carrying buckets.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Please note: the north car park will be closed from Monday to Wednesday for repainting. Staff can park in the south car park or take the free bus from the station. We apologise for any trouble.
options: The south car park will be closed for three days.
The company is asking staff to help paint the north car park.
A free bus will replace all parking at the office.
A notice tells staff about a temporary parking change and other ways to arrive.
quests.correctAnswer: A notice tells staff about a temporary parking change and other ways to arrive.
quests.hint: What does a notice want the reader to know or do?
quests.explanation: The notice announces a short closure and offers two alternatives, so it is helping staff plan. The other options invent duties or permanent changes that are not mentioned.
keyPoints: The north car park is closed from Monday to Wednesday.
Staff can use the south car park or a free station bus.
The notice apologises for the inconvenience.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: The gym will open one hour earlier starting next month. Members who like to work out before the office can now begin at five. The change is a trial, and the manager wants to hear members' opinions.
options: The gym is trying earlier opening hours and wants feedback.
The manager has decided to keep the new hours for ever.
The gym will close one hour earlier from next month.
All gym members must now exercise before going to the office.
quests.correctAnswer: The gym is trying earlier opening hours and wants feedback.
quests.hint: Small words such as 'trial' matter. Check that your answer does not turn a possibility into a certainty.
quests.explanation: The earlier opening is described as a trial, so the manager is still asking for opinions. The wrong choices treat it as a rule or a permanent decision.
keyPoints: The gym will open at five, one hour earlier than before.
Early risers can now exercise before work.
The change is only a trial, and the manager wants opinions.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Reminder for parents: Sports Day is on Friday, and children should wear their team T-shirts. Please bring water bottles and sun hats because there is little shade on the field. Lunch will be served at noon.
options: Children must buy new team T-shirts before Friday.
Sports Day will move indoors because of hot weather.
A school explains what children need for Sports Day.
Parents will join the races on the field this year.
quests.correctAnswer: A school explains what children need for Sports Day.
quests.hint: Read the notice as a whole: what is the writer trying to help parents do?
quests.explanation: Every sentence tells parents how to get children ready for the day: clothes, water, hats and lunch timing. The alternatives invent changes that the notice never announces.
keyPoints: Sports Day takes place on Friday.
Children should wear team shirts and bring water and sun hats.
Lunch will be served at noon.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Miguel's old phone took photos slowly and ran out of battery by noon. His new phone takes clear pictures at once and lasts all day. He is glad he switched.
options: Miguel's old phone lasts all day but takes slow photos.
Miguel photographed his old phone at noon.
Miguel bought a new phone because the old one broke.
Miguel's new phone works better than his old one.
quests.correctAnswer: Miguel's new phone works better than his old one.
quests.hint: In a comparison, check which item is described as better. Some options swap them.
quests.explanation: The paragraph sets an old, slow phone against a new, reliable one. One wrong option reverses the comparison, and another invents the reason for buying.
keyPoints: Miguel's old phone was slow and its battery died early.
His new phone takes clear photos quickly and lasts all day.
He is happy he changed phones.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Both of Dana's jobs are in cafés, but they feel very different. The morning shop is quiet and mostly serves regular customers, while the weekend place is loud and full of tourists. She likes the calm one more, though the weekend job pays better.
options: Dana works only in the weekend café, which pays better.
Dana works in two very different cafés and prefers the quiet one.
Dana serves tourists in cafés all over the city.
Dana prefers the weekend café because of its loud atmosphere.
quests.correctAnswer: Dana works in two very different cafés and prefers the quiet one.
quests.hint: With two things being compared, the summary should include both and the writer's preference.
quests.explanation: The paragraph contrasts a calm morning café with a noisy weekend one and says Dana likes the calm one better. Wrong options either drop one job or reverse her preference.
keyPoints: Dana works in two different cafés.
One is quiet with regulars, and the other is loud with tourists.
She prefers the quiet one, even though the other pays better.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ella grew up drinking tea slowly with friends. In her new city, most people grab coffee in paper cups and hurry to work. She misses the old habit but has started to enjoy coffee too.
options: Ella has stopped drinking tea because she prefers coffee.
Ella opens a tea shop in her new city.
Ella compares slow tea with friends and quick city coffee.
Ella's friends drink coffee in paper cups every day.
quests.correctAnswer: Ella compares slow tea with friends and quick city coffee.
quests.hint: Find the two things being set side by side and note how the writer feels about each.
quests.explanation: The paragraph contrasts two drinking cultures and shows Ella's mixed feelings. Saying she has stopped drinking tea ignores that she misses it.
keyPoints: Ella is used to drinking tea slowly with friends.
In her new city, people drink coffee quickly on the way to work.
She misses the old way but is beginning to like coffee.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: On her first day at the bakery, Grace burned two trays of rolls and forgot the price of a loaf. Her manager smiled and said everyone makes mistakes at the start. By closing time, Grace felt more confident.
options: Grace's manager was angry about the burned rolls.
Grace's difficult first day at work ended with her feeling more confident.
Grace forgot the price of a loaf on her first day.
Grace has worked at the bakery for many years.
quests.correctAnswer: Grace's difficult first day at work ended with her feeling more confident.
quests.hint: Look at how the paragraph ends. A summary should follow the change in the person's feelings.
quests.explanation: The story starts with mistakes and ends with more confidence, thanks to a kind manager. A single mistake, like the price of a loaf, is only one part of that story.
keyPoints: Grace made several mistakes on her first day at the bakery.
Her manager reassured her that this is normal.
She felt more confident by the end of the day.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Hamid nearly gave up learning the piano after months of mistakes. Then his teacher asked him to play only one short piece perfectly. That small success made him want to keep practising.
options: Hamid plays the piano only when he wants to relax.
Hamid learned many pieces quickly with his teacher.
One small success helped Hamid keep learning the piano.
Hamid's teacher stopped his lessons after months of mistakes.
quests.correctAnswer: One small success helped Hamid keep learning the piano.
quests.hint: Ask what changed Hamid's mind. That turning point usually sits in the middle of the paragraph.
quests.explanation: The teacher's simple task gave Hamid a success that kept him going after months of difficulty. The wrong options invent lessons ending or rapid progress.
keyPoints: Hamid almost quit the piano after many mistakes.
His teacher gave him one short piece to perfect.
Succeeding at it made him want to continue.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Before her first English class abroad, Sofia was afraid of speaking. She sat at the back and stayed silent for a week. Then a classmate invited her for coffee, and talking became much easier.
options: A classmate's invitation helped nervous Sofia start talking.
Sofia's teacher moved her to the front to make her speak.
Sofia moved abroad to work in a coffee shop.
Sofia enjoyed sitting silently at the back of the class.
quests.correctAnswer: A classmate's invitation helped nervous Sofia start talking.
quests.hint: Track how Sofia's situation changes from the first sentence to the last.
quests.explanation: Sofia begins silent and afraid, and a friendly invitation begins to change that. Any option that adds a teacher's action or a new job goes beyond the text.
keyPoints: Sofia was afraid to speak in her English class abroad.
She stayed silent at the back for a week.
A classmate's invitation to coffee made talking easier.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: To make a paper boat, Noor folds a sheet in half and turns down the two top corners. Next she folds the bottom edges upward on both sides. When she pulls the shape open, a small boat appears.
options: Noor demonstrates the steps for folding a paper boat.
Noor folds a sheet of paper in half.
Noor teaches children how to draw a boat.
Noor floats a paper boat across a river.
quests.correctAnswer: Noor demonstrates the steps for folding a paper boat.
quests.hint: For steps, the summary should name the whole process and its final result.
quests.explanation: The passage lists steps that end in a finished paper boat. Only mentioning the first fold names one step, not the process.
keyPoints: Noor is making a paper boat.
She folds the paper in half, turns corners and folds the edges.
Pulling the shape open reveals the finished boat.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Chef Amadou begins the day by checking the fish that arrives at the market. Then he chooses the best pieces and plans the menu around them. By evening, his guests are eating dishes made from that morning's catch.
options: Chef Amadou changes the guests' meals when they complain.
Chef Amadou checks the fish at the market each morning.
Chef Amadou cooks fish for guests at a market stall.
Chef Amadou builds each day's menu around the freshest fish he finds.
quests.correctAnswer: Chef Amadou builds each day's menu around the freshest fish he finds.
quests.hint: Choose the answer that shows how the morning choices lead to the evening meal.
quests.explanation: The paragraph connects the morning fish inspection with the evening menu. Focusing only on the market visit skips the point that the fish decides what is served.
keyPoints: Chef Amadou inspects the fish at the market every morning.
He picks the best pieces and designs the menu around them.
His guests eat the dishes that evening.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Farah uploads a video to her class page every Sunday. First she records a short talk, then she adds captions, and finally she checks the sound. Her classmates watch it before Monday's lesson.
options: Farah checks the sound quality on all school videos.
Farah prepares and shares a weekly video for her class.
Farah's classmates make a video for her every Sunday.
Farah adds captions to videos for her teacher.
quests.correctAnswer: Farah prepares and shares a weekly video for her class.
quests.hint: See how the steps fit into one routine, and who the video is for.
quests.explanation: Recording, captioning and checking sound are the steps she follows to give her classmates a video before class. Choosing only one step misses the sharing purpose.
keyPoints: Farah shares a video with her class every Sunday.
She records, adds captions and checks the sound.
Classmates watch it before Monday's lesson.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Ms. Kalinin's neighbourhood library was losing visitors, so she started a Saturday story hour for children. Parents began arriving with their kids, and many of them also borrowed books. Within three months, visitor numbers had doubled.
options: Visitor numbers doubled because the library bought new books.
A Saturday story hour brought more visitors to a library.
Many parents borrowed books during the story hour.
Ms. Kalinin closed the library on Saturdays for the children.
quests.correctAnswer: A Saturday story hour brought more visitors to a library.
quests.hint: A strong summary joins the problem, the action and the result.
quests.explanation: A library with fewer visitors tried a story hour and gained many more. One wrong option is a small detail, and another gives a cause the passage never mentions.
keyPoints: The neighbourhood library was losing visitors.
Ms. Kalinin started a Saturday story hour for children.
Parents came too, and visitor numbers doubled in three months.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A small clothes shop in Lagos was struggling to reach new customers. The owner, Tola, began showing outfits on social media and answering questions through messages. Sales rose steadily, and she hired a second assistant.
options: Social media helped a small clothes shop find customers and grow.
Social media made Tola's shop lose many of its customers.
Tola hired a second assistant to answer questions in the shop.
Tola closed her shop in Lagos and now sells only online.
quests.correctAnswer: Social media helped a small clothes shop find customers and grow.
quests.hint: Look for a problem, what was done about it, and what happened next.
quests.explanation: The shop needed customers, used social media, and grew as a result. The assistant is only one sign of that growth, and the last option reverses the outcome.
keyPoints: Tola's clothes shop was not reaching new customers.
She started showing outfits and answering questions online.
Sales increased, and she hired another assistant.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Tomas wanted to improve his running time before the town race. He trained four mornings a week and ate more vegetables. On race day, he finished twelve minutes faster than last year.
options: Tomas eats vegetables every morning before races.
Tomas ran the town race for the first time this year.
Tomas trained regularly and improved his race time.
Tomas won first prize at the town race.
quests.correctAnswer: Tomas trained regularly and improved his race time.
quests.hint: Join the goal, the effort and the result into one idea.
quests.explanation: Tomas set a goal, trained and got a better time than the year before. An option about vegetables picks a small habit, and the others add facts that are not given.
keyPoints: Tomas wanted to run faster in the town race.
He trained four mornings a week and improved his diet.
He finished twelve minutes faster than the previous year.
